October, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:50896

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice B. P. Sharma

On The 8 th Of October, 2025
 Criminal Appeal No. 1836 of 2017
 Arun Kumar Kuswaha
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Sudhanshu Singh- Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Lalitendra Pratap Singh- Advocate for the compla
 Shri Manoj Kushwaha- Panel Lawyer for respondent/Stat
 Order

This appeal has been filed under Section 374(2) of CrPC, 1973 against the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 06.04.2017 delivered in S.T. No.04/2015 ( State of MP Vs. Arun Kumar ) by the learned Special Judge, Special Judge, Singrauli (MP) by which the appellant was convicted for offence under section 5(L) r/w Section 6 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for ten years and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/-, with default stipulation.

sentences.text: 2. Relevant facts, briefly stated are that on the basis of report lodged, crime was registered against the appellant at Police Station Vindhyanagar, District Singrauli for commission of offence punishable under Sections 366, 376(2), 506 of IPC and under Section 4/6 of POCSO Act.
After completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed before the competent Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50896 2 CRA-1836-2017 3.

After recording the statements of prosecution witnesses and appreciating the evidence led by parties, learned trial Court found the appellants guilty for commission of offence punishable under Section 5(L) r/w Section 6 of POCSO Act and sentenced them as mentioned above.
Being aggrieved with the impugned judgment, the appellant has preferred this criminal appeal before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant expressly gave up his challenge to the findings of the Court below so far as the conviction of the appellant is concerned.
In other words, learned counsel for the appellant accepted the findings of conviction passed against the appellant, however, he challenged the quantum of punishment alone.

Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that in the Arun Kumar Kuswaha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134107685/
1 instant case, parties have compromised the matter which has been verified by Registrar J-II.

sentences.text: The verification report dated 24.09.2025 is brought on record.
Appellant was in custody for approximately 10 months during trial and after the judgment of Trial Court.
He further submits that appellant and victim have married and they were living as husband and wife before the incident also.
Marriage between them was solemnized before the incident.
They were blessed with a daughter.
This fact can be verified by the statement of the victim as recorded before the Trial Court.

Thus having regard to all the circumstances which resulted in appellant's conviction and further keeping in view the fact that the appellant was facing the prosecution since the year 2015, jail sentence of appellant may be reduced suitably.
5.

Learned counsel for the respondent/State has submitted that after appreciating the evidence produced by the prosecution, the Court below have NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:50896 3 CRA-1836-2017 rightly found the appellant guilty for the aforesaid offence, therefore, no grounds are available for reducing the jail sentence awarded to the appellants,
hence, he prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
Since learned counsel for the appellant has not pressed this appeal on merits, the facts of the case need not be elaborated herein.
7. Turning to the point of compromise, it is also significant to note that the compromise has been filed at the stage of appeal before this Court.

On this aspect, it would be relevant to note the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ishwar Singh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh [AIR 2009 SC 675] , wherein the Apex Court has observed as under:
"15.

entities.text: Ishwar Singh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh [AIR 2009 SC 675]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In our considered opinion, it would not be appropriate to order compounding of an offence not compoundable under the code ignoring and keeping aside statutory provisions.

In our judgment, however, limited submission of the learned counsel for the appellant deserves consideration that while imposing substantive sentence, the factum of compromise between the parties is indeed a relevant circumstances which,
the Court may keep in mind."

8 . On this point, the view of Hon'ble Apex Court in the Unnikrishnan alias Unnikuttan versus State of Kerala reported in AIR 2017 Supreme Court 1745 is also worth referring in the context of this case as under:-
"10.

In series of decisions i.e. Bharath Singh vs. State of M.P. and Ors., 1990 (Supp)
SCC 62, Ramlal vs. State of J & K, (1999) 2 SCC 213, Puttaswamy vs. State of Karnataka and Anr, (2009) 1 SCC 71 1, this Court NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:50896 4 CRA-1836-2017 allowed the parties to compound the offence even though the offence is a non-compoundable depending on the facts and circumstances of each case.

What emerges from the above is that even if an offence is not compoundable within the scope of Section 320 of Code of Criminal Procedure the Court may, in view of the compromise arrive at between the parties, reduce the sentence imposed while maintaining the conviction."
9.

In the case of Murali vs. State; (2021) 1 SCC 726 , Hon'ble the Apex Court has held that the fact of amicable settlement/compromise between the parties can be a relevant factor for the purpose of reduction in quantum of sentence of convicts even in serious non-compoundable offences.

10. In the case of Unnikrishnan alias Unnikuttan (supra) it is held as under :-
"10.

In series of decisions i.e. Bharath Singh vs. State of M.P. and Ors., 1990 (Supp)
SCC 62, Ramlal vs. State of J & K, (1999) 2 SCC 213, Puttaswamy vs. State of Karnataka and Anr, (2009) 1 SCC 71 1, this Court allowed the parties to compound the offence even though the offence is a non compoundable depending on the facts and circumstances of each case.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In some cases this Court while imposing the fine amount reduced the sentence to the period already undergone.

What emerges from the above is that even if an offence is not compoundable within the scope of Section 320 of Code of Criminal Procedure the Court may, in view of the compromise arrive at between the parties, reduce the sentence imposed while maintaining the conviction."
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50896 5 CRA-1836-2017 11.
It is seen that the parties have compromised the matter, which has been duly verified.

It is true that the offences registered against the appellant are not compoundable under the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, therefore, the application for compromise cannot be allowed.

However, as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in aforementioned case laws, in exceptional circumstances, considering the voluntary settlement between the parties, the Court may give effect to such compromise at the stage of final disposal of appeal and further that where parties have amicably resolved their disputes and the complainant has unequivocally supported the compromise,
the Court may, in the interest of justice and to maintain social harmony, modify the relief suitably by reducing the substantive sentence.
12.

Thus, though the offences registered against the appellant is non compoundable, however,
considering the fact that the appellant and the victim have married and are living as husband and wife with their daughter as well as the fact that the compromise has voluntarily been entered into between the parties and the complainant has no objection to compounding the offence, and the period of incarceration already undergone by the appellant, I am of the considered opinion that the ends of justice would be met if the conviction of the appellant under Section 5(L) r/w Section 6 of POCSO Act is maintained, but the sentence of imprisonment awarded is reduced to the period already undergone by him.

sentences.text: Resultantly, the conviction of the appellant under Section 5(L) r/w Section 6 of POCSO Act, as recorded by the learned Trial Court, is hereby affirmed.
The substantive sentence of imprisonment awarded to the appellant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50896 6 CRA-1836-2017 is reduced to the period already undergone by him.
The appellant, being on bail, his bail bonds stand discharged.
14. The appeal is allowed in part to the extent indicated above.

15. Let a copy of this judgment be sent to the concerned trial Court for information and necessary compliance.
